question_type: statistic over the 12 monthly values of one fiscal year (Type-7 quartile spread) with a question-prescribed intermediate rounding; unit conversion millions->tenths of billions; FY month membership; rounding tie at the hundredths
decisive_step: Unresolved: the reference and all seven arms (a, b, c, v8 none/prompt/cards, opus) are wrong. The data step is not in doubt: the 12 FY2021 month rows of FFO-2 'On-Budget and Off-Budget Receipts by Source', column 'Corporation > Net (7)', treasury_bulletin_2021_12.txt:524-535 (worklog Step 4; the Sep 2020 row at line 523 belongs to FY2020 and is excluded; calc.py asserts the 12 months sum to the FY-to-date line 536; Step 5 finds no revisions in any later issue). The decisive step is therefore the computation convention: the reference read 'intermediate values rounded to the tenths of billions' as rounding each monthly value before Type-7 quartiles (worklog Step 6-7) and logged three alternatives in calc.py (no rounding; raw data with the quartiles rounded to tenths; both rounded). Cells a and c submitted the two tie-rounding variants of the reference's primary reading (one hundredth apart) and both were graded wrong, so the key follows some other reading - most plausibly rounding the quartiles themselves, or a different H-spread/quartile convention - which cannot be identified without the key.

notes: (1) Parser header shift on FFO-2 in 2022_12 (a[14]) and 2022_03 (c[63]): a spurious trailing label shifts the corporation columns' names ('Net income taxes > Net (7)', 'Employment and general retirement > Net (7)'); the identity note (c5 = c6 + c7) pins them, but a rejected the table on the label text alone (a[15]) and lost 35 steps; the 2021_12 printing has clean labels. Fixing the header parser or printing 'label unreliable, identity says Corporation' next to shifted columns would have shortened a and c drastically. (2) The quarterly capsule tables 'N-Quarter Net Budget Receipts by Source, Fiscal Year 2021' (values already in billions to tenths - the likely origin of the question's 'intermediate values rounded to the tenths of billions') are indexed as continuation parts of narrative 'tables' with titles like 'Estate and gift taxes-Net estate ...' (a[33], c[20]), have no table id for printings (c[30]), and the Dec issue has no Q4 capsule (a[49], c[27]). (3) show_table --grep with a year string excludes the FY months dated the previous calendar year (a[50], c[58]); an FY-aware filter is the natural tool change. (4) calc: numpy Type-7 on tenths-rounded inputs gave an exact half at the hundredths and float round() printed the lower neighbour (a[59], c[65]); the reference's review predicted exactly this split. (5) b's gate: the ledger links calc literals to tool output by text, so in-head unit conversion (millions -> tenths of billions) plus a dropped sign produced one false binding (a 2017 capsule cell) and one false 'ungrounded' finding, while the real 13-input error passed; the v10 gate needs scale-aware matching (x/1000 rounded to 1 dp) before more rules are added. (6) All three cells and the reference used numpy's 'linear' method; nobody tried Tukey hinges or rounding the quartiles, so the graded-correct reading is undetermined from these materials.
